title: Flute
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS flute (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: A Boehm concert flute assembled from published data: hole positions, bore, head-joint taper, cork and mouth-hole from Boehm's 1871 treatise as recomputed and measured by Miller (1922), the embouchure riser of a measured Pearl PF-661 from UNSW, and the player's mouth pressure and jet length from a published experienced-flautist measurement (de la Cuadra et al. 2008). All sixteen holes are in the model, closed ones as hard-closed chimneys; the three notes use the published simple fingerings. Nothing was fitted to the Iowa recordings. With the jet-island phase fix and a lip-jet card whose band is placed by the published Strouhal number of maximum jet amplification, D4 and G4 now sound their first register natively, with the same pitch for two jet seeds. A5, which needs the second register, sounds an octave low. It is a hybrid description, not one real flute, and the lip-jet card is a published-parameter estimate, not a measured card.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing-pressure gesture, with the lip geometry, jet length and the mouth contraction law, acting on a connected duct network (fs-couple network performance, one jet drives the whole graph)

16 tone-hole branches as plane-wave chimney sections on ideal junctions, open or closed per fingering, with the published head-joint taper as stacked cylinders, the cork cavity and the embouchure riser
fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on every section of the network (moist air at the published measurement state)

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the graded sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end, with every open aperture and the embouchure summed at the receiver (the computed mutual operator could not be used, see below)

a jet source whose amplification band is a magnitude and whose phase is the convective delay alone (island fix 1718d79fb), driven by a published-parameter lip-jet card (theta/b 1.75, convection ratio 0.4; X-Est, not a measured card): the first register speaks at the played Strouhal numbers
physics_missing: a measured lip jet: the opt-in published jet transfer (Price, Johnston and McKinnon 2015, with a measured phase velocity) was NOT run on this flute, because its control, the tin-whistle ladder at the paper's flows, did not self-sustain (all four renders silent, gate 2 of pexfp.320). The lip jet is classed a short channel (de la Cuadra 2005 Sec. 3.1, decided before any flute ramp), and the playing-condition jet gain is UNKNOWN (u-jet-playing-gain)
a tone-hole model beyond a plane-wave chimney on an ideal junction: no matching-volume or end-correction treatment of the junction, no pad cups, no undercut

a broadband, mutually coupled radiation model: the computed operator admits at most eight openings and is fitted to the mechanics Nyquist, where its baffled-piston quadrature fails at the clock this flute needs; the compact load holds only for ka up to 0.5 and so limits the receiver band to about 2.8 kHz, far below the flute's harmonic content; the holes also sit on a cylinder in the real flute but are placed in a flat baffle plane here

frequency-dependent loss above 3 kHz, and any loss in the tone-hole chimneys and the riser: the viscothermal cell needs rate of about fifty times its band edge, so loss is selected only on bore sections of 17 mm or more and only to 3 kHz
the true head-joint taper profile (only the two published endpoints are known; it is a stack of cylinders on a straight line between them) and a convergence ladder on that stacking

a flutist's lip jet: the jet card in use is an inline estimate for a lip jet built from published parameters, not a measured card, the jet displacement gain is the demonstrator value, the labium offset is another player's measured reference jet (Onogi 2021, one player, +0.29 +- 0.30 mm), the jet angle is already inside that offset, and the onset ramp is authored
breath-warmed bore gas: the bore is at the UNSW measurement state, which sits flat of a played flute
a same-specimen impedance pair, so the passive chain is checked only against the pooled UNSW statements, not against a measured impedance of this flute
wall and pad vibration, fork fingerings (F sharp, B flat), vibrato, and the register-hole and trill-hole notes

the overblown register transition: not reproduced. Natively the first register persists up to the strongest jet tried, at every step count of the gate's rate ladder, and the level at that strongest jet still changes with the step count, so that regime is not converged. The published octave jump (de la Cuadra 2008) is therefore not claimed, and the second-register note (A5) sounds the first register of its fingering, an octave low. An earlier Python mirror showed isolated higher-register points that moved with the sample rate; the native runs do not, so those were a mirror artifact. A card-by-geometry test (the same pressure sweep or measured flows, with the jet card swapped on a fixed geometry) shows that whether the registers stage follows the jet card, not the geometry: the lip-jet card does not stage on the flute geometry nor on the tin-whistle geometry, while the windway-jet card stages the whistle at its measured flows. So the missing overblow of the flute points at its lip-jet card, an estimate, and not at its bore or holes. The windway-jet card is no substitute: on the flute geometry it sounds high partials of the pipe at the playing pressure

a spectrum like a real flute: with one player's measured labium offset (+0.29 mm) the cut is asymmetric and the even harmonics sound, H2 25 to 28 dB below H1 and H4 and H6 8 to 18 dB below it; across that player's -0.01 to +0.59 mm, H2/H1 spans -58 to -19 dB and the pitch moves at most 0.21 cents. With the demonstrator gain the jet swings 35 to 62 jet half-widths at the labium, so the cut stays nearly a square wave and the upper harmonics stay strong; the radiation band is also capped by the compact load

a pitch claim: the notes land within tens of cents of equal temperament, but my independent plane-wave check puts the passive bore resonances sharp by an amount that grows with the number of open holes (missing tone-hole corrections, lip occlusion of the embouchure), so the jet loading and these missing terms decide the pitch, not a verified model

native verification beyond two notes: the jet-island fix is verified natively on D4 and G4 at one mechanics clock and two jet seeds, and on a plain pipe at three mechanics clocks (tests/flue_jet_phase.rs: same lock, level within a few percent); the flute itself has not been rendered at more than one clock, because its viscothermal loss cells fix the clock

a jet island that reproduces the overblowing ladder of the edge-tone gates: the gates were moved from the interim slot-jet card, which is outside its own validity band at every row, to the lip-jet card (gate change 5d77b0a49). Natively the cut-up direction gate (cut-ups taken from the published first-register window, a longer cut-up locks the same or a lower register) and the labium-duty gate hold. The overblowing-ladder gate is RED: no pressure of the sweep locks the second register and the first register persists to the strongest jet, the same finding as the overblown-register item above. The linear loop analysis agrees with the native rows at low pressure (the lowest rows are linearly stable, the next are barely unstable and oscillate only at tiny amplitude). At the top of the sweep it gives the second register the larger linear margin, but both registers are far above threshold and the first register's saturated cycle persists, with a cold start as well as with a ramp. Diagnosis from time-domain mirror runs and the native diagnostics: the island's authored displacement gain, set from the inviscid linear-stability maximum, swings the jet by many jet half-widths at the labium, so the labium switches like a hard relay and the established first-register cycle fixes the switching times. Compressing the deflection does not change that and an amplitude-dependent labium loss does not either; lowering the gain does move the register boundary, so the missing physics is a measured, viscous-limited jet amplification (profile broadening along the cut-up). It needs a cited amplification value that has not been obtained, so the gain is left unchanged. The interim-card gates were green before the phase fix and red after it, and that old green is not evidence that the original island was right
